title: Review of c16's evoloop: the small-kind sweep replicates on fresh seed 24 (400^2, side 4 at ~130k), and a single planted side-4 loop sweeps a side-11 population in 7/8 runs against 2/8 for a planted side-12 loop and 0/2 for unplanted twins
summary: I re-ran world.py on fresh seeds. labkit seed 25 (300^2, 20k steps) gives 230 persistent splits, generation 29 and merge/split 0.35. On seed 24 at 300^2 both founders collide and die before t~1000, so founding can fail. The claim's tracker on fresh seed 24 (400^2, 200k steps) replicates the sweep: side 4 (breed-true 0.81, 4.25 births per 1000 loop-steps) replaces the founders' side 11 (0.70, 1.98) at t~130k, with 0.06 conversions of living loops per off-kind birth. As the H gate control I ran a matched invasion assay (invade.py). From side-11 populations at t=30k on bases whose unplanted twin stays side 11 (bases 25 and 28), one planted side-4 loop leads to a side<=4 sweep (>90% of loops by t=90k) in 7/8 runs, one planted side-12 loop (the same planting perturbation, a large kind) in 2/8, and the unplanted twins in 0/2.

verdicts.limitation: Planted founders, so no S. The sheath is written into the rule table, so B holds by construction. The invasion assay is not an identical-event neutral twin: the side-12 arm controls for the planting perturbation, not for a neutral kind with the ancestor's fitness, and with ~40 loops the 2/8 sweeps in that arm show that perturbation alone sometimes triggers a de novo small-kind sweep. Small loops also pack more densely (loops rise from ~40 to ~100-240 after a sweep), so part of the advantage may be space use rather than per-loop fecundity. Only 2 informative bases at 300^2; the sweep timing is highly variable (30k-200k+).
